title: _assert_finite_glm_record silently accepts None/missing required GLM fields; only a bare assert guards them, so malformed records raise AssertionError (or TypeError under -O) instead of ModelExplanationError
description: `_as_float` short-circuits `None` to `None` BEFORE the strict branch (lines 25-26), so `_as_float(value, strict=True)` raises ModelExplanationError only for non-numeric/non-finite values, never for `None`. `_assert_finite_glm_record` validates every required numeric field via `_as_float(record.get(field), strict=True)` (lines 317-318) and discards the result. Because `record.get(field)` returns `None` when the key is absent or explicitly null, a GLM record that is MISSING `base_value`/`sum_contributions`/`prediction_from_contributions`/`prediction_value` (or carries an explicit `None`) passes `_assert_finite_glm_record` without error, despite its name/docstring asserting finiteness. Downstream, `explain_rustystats_glm_prediction` re-parses these fields with `strict=True`, gets `None`, and the ONLY thing catching it is a bare `assert ... is not None` (lines 386, 458, 459, 460; also 420 for each contribution). That assert raises `AssertionError` — not the module-contract `ModelExplanationError` — and is stripped entirely when Python runs under `-O`/PYTHONOPTIMIZE, in which case `_prediction_tolerance(None)` -> `abs(None)` raises `TypeError`. The whole module is documented/built to fail with `ModelExplanationError`, and the sole production caller `enrich_model_score` (src/haute/_trace_enrichment.py:712) catches ONLY `ModelExplanationError` to emit structured per-method error metadata via `explanation_error_metadata_for_config`. An `AssertionError`/`TypeError` instead falls through to the broad `except Exception` (line 725), producing a generic 'model score enrichment failed' detail with `prediction_value=None` and `error_type='AssertionError'` — an observable degradation of the trace for a malformed-record case the validation function exists specifically to handle cleanly.
evidence: _as_float: line 25 `if value is None: return None` executes before the strict finite check (33-36), so strict=True returns None for None input rather than raising. _assert_finite_glm_record (317-318) does `_as_float(record.get(field), field_name=field, strict=True)` with no presence check -> a missing/None `sum_contributions` is not rejected. explain_rustystats_glm_prediction line 447-460 then: `sum_contributions = _as_float(record.get('sum_contributions'), strict=True)` (=None) ; `assert sum_contributions is not None` -> AssertionError, not ModelExplanationError. _trace_enrichment.enrich_model_score line 712 `except _model_explainability.ModelExplanationError` does not catch AssertionError; broad `except Exception` at 725 produces the generic failure detail.
